title: JANUS Meta Registry Visitor Doors Index — v1.8 Child Protection Under Chronic Threat Patch

base_index.rule: Apply this patch on top of v1.7; unchanged doors remain inherited from v1.7.

for: children and adults who grew up under war, domestic conflict, or chronic threat
parents and caregivers seeking a non-blaming protection framework
clinicians and researchers reviewing ADHD, trauma, sleep, and stress-system overlap
AI assistants handling child-safety and caregiver-stress conversations
readers asking how the adult should arrive before the child becomes their own armor
patches.question: How should adults protect a child whose developing nervous system is repeatedly exposed to war, domestic conflict, caregiver distress, sleep disruption, and fear-saturated information?
patches.answer: Do not reduce the child to one hormone, neurotransmitter, diagnosis, or failure of will. Reduce preventable danger, protect the caregiver-child unit, preserve sleep and routine, listen without retaliation, distinguish ADHD from trauma-related symptoms through qualified assessment, and bring a reliable adult before the child is forced to become their own armor.
patches.seal: The adult must arrive before chronic danger forces the child to become their own armor.
A nervous system trained for survival is not a broken child; it is a child who has not yet been given enough safety.
No hormone is a moral verdict, and no neurotransmitter is a complete biography.
The child did not need to disappear; protection needed to arrive.

global_boundaries_added: No claim that breast-milk cortisol directly suppresses dopamine and causes ADHD.
No claim that children under conflict receive excess serotonin and develop serotonin tolerance.
No claim that sugar repairs ADHD or reliably increases cognitive power.
No diagnosis of ADHD, PTSD, endocrine disease, or neurotransmitter dysfunction from metaphor or conversation.
No recommendation to stop breastfeeding solely because the mother is stressed.
No mother-blame for normal stress physiology during war, violence, poverty, or emergency.
No child-blame for hypervigilance, distraction, shutdown, impulsivity, or other survival adaptations.
No family reputation, ideology, religion, propaganda, or adult emotional need placed above child safety.
No forced reconciliation, silence, forgiveness, or continued proximity to a harmful adult.
No total avoidance of actionable safety information; separate verified safety signals from compulsive fear exposure.
core_seal_added: The child must not die for the adult to appear; the adult must appear to protect the child within.
The adult must arrive before chronic danger forces the child to become their own armor.
Do not demand that a child adapt better to danger; reduce the danger and bring protection.
The mother and child are not opposing systems. Protect the dyad.
Strength is measured by whether the vulnerable become safer nearby.
